## Q: Who are Modern Curtains and Blinds?

Modern Curtains and Blinds is a family-owned Melbourne window-furnishings business owned by Deane and Dee. Based in Preston, Victoria, the business measures, supplies and installs custom curtains, blinds, plantation shutters, security doors, fly screens and awnings across the greater Melbourne metropolitan area. The business is Australian Made and Owned. Phone 1300 732 319.

## Q: What suburbs of Melbourne do you service?

Modern Curtains and Blinds operates from Preston (postcode 3072) and services Melbourne suburbs within roughly a 30 km service radius. This includes (but is not limited to): Preston, Northcote, Brunswick, Coburg, Reservoir, Thornbury, Carlton, Fitzroy, Heidelberg, Bundoora, Ivanhoe, Kew, Hawthorn, Richmond, Doncaster, Templestowe, Eltham, Greensborough, Diamond Creek and Mernda. The full live list is published at https://www.moderncurtainsandblinds.com.au/sitemap.xml.

## Q: How does the free in-home measure and quote work?

Customers submit a short enquiry at https://www.moderncurtainsandblinds.com.au/quote or call 1300 732 319. Within 24 hours, Deane or Dee personally calls back to organise an in-home appointment at a time that suits the customer. At the appointment, fabric samples and product options are brought to the home, every opening is measured, and a detailed written quote is produced. There is no obligation, no pressure and no upsell scripting.

## Q: What products do you sell?

- **Custom curtains** — sheer, blockout, double (sheer + blockout layered), S-fold, Wavefold, velvet, motorised options.
- **Custom blinds** — roller blinds (blockout, sunscreen, translucent), honeycomb (cellular) blinds, Venetian blinds, panel glide blinds, Roman blinds, soft vertical drapes (Veri Shades).
- **Plantation shutters** — interior basswood and PVC; exterior aluminium shutters.
- **Security doors and screens** — heavy-duty mesh, decorative wrought-iron-style, pet-resistant mesh.
- **Fly screens** — window screens and door screens, retractable options available.
- **Awnings** — auto-awnings, folding-arm awnings, drop-arm awnings, retractable awnings.
- **Motorisation** — Somfy and equivalent motors for curtains, blinds and awnings, with optional smart-home integration.

## Q: How much does it cost?

The in-home measure and quote is free with no obligation. Final pricing depends on the product, fabric, dimensions of the openings and any motorisation. Modern Curtains and Blinds offers competitive Melbourne pricing and provides a clear written quote at the appointment so the customer can compare with confidence.

## Q: How much heat does a home lose through its windows?

Glass is the weakest thermal point of almost every Australian home — a single pane insulates
poorly compared with an insulated wall. Up to 40% of a home's heating energy can be lost
through its windows in winter, and bare glass is also the main path for unwanted heat gain in
summer. Covering the glass properly with lined curtains or close-fitting blinds is the fastest
and cheapest way to close that gap, and far cheaper than replacing the glazing itself. Full
guide: https://www.moderncurtainsandblinds.com.au/guides/energy-efficient-curtains-blinds-melbourne

## Q: Do blockout curtains actually keep heat in during winter?

Yes — meaningfully. A lined blockout curtain traps a layer of still air between the fabric and
the glass, and still air is one of the best insulators there is. The catch is coverage: the
curtain needs to run wider than the window frame, drop below the sill (to the floor is better)
and sit close to the glass. A skimpy curtain that floats mid-air with gaps around every edge
lets warm room air slide behind it, chill against the glass and pour back out the bottom, so a
poorly fitted curtain can do very little. Fit is most of the result — which is why Modern
Curtains and Blinds measures in the home rather than selling off a shelf.

## Q: What are the best blinds to keep a Melbourne home warm?

Honeycomb (cellular) blinds are the strongest insulating blind — their hexagon cells trap air
in pockets across the whole window. A quality blockout roller blind, measured snug inside the
reveal so the gaps around the edges are small, is the value pick and delivers a lot of the same
benefit for less. A double roller adds a sunscreen layer for daytime use, and layering any
blind with a curtain over the top performs better than either alone. What matters more than the
product name is the fit: a blind with daylight showing around all four edges is barely
insulating anything.

## Q: What do window coverings need in order to actually insulate?

- Curtains fitted wider than the window frame and dropping to the floor where the room allows.
- Blinds measured snug inside the reveal so edge gaps are minimal.
- A pelmet, or a closed-off track top, so warm air cannot dive in over the rail and circulate
  down the cold glass — the most commonly overlooked detail.
- Coverings closed at dusk while the heating is running; opened during the day to let winter
  sun in.
- Layering (blind at the glass plus a lined curtain over it) for the best-performing windows.

## Q: Are honeycomb blinds worth the extra cost over roller blinds?

It depends on the room. Honeycomb cells trap air across the glass and are the best insulating
blind available. But a well-made blockout roller, measured tight to the opening, closes most of
the same gap at a lower price. For a bedroom used every night on a cold side of the house,
honeycombs earn their keep; for a spare room, a snug blockout roller is the smarter spend.
Modern Curtains and Blinds supplies both.

## Q: Do motorised blinds save energy?

Motorisation is a convenience product first — remotes, schedules, app and voice control — not
an insulation product. Where it helps in winter is timing: a schedule that closes every blind
and curtain at dusk means the insulation is actually deployed before the evening chill,
whether anyone is home or not. Choose motorisation for the convenience; the warmth discipline
is a bonus.

## Q: Is it worth improving a Melbourne home instead of selling right now?

Melbourne dwelling values have been flat to slightly lower through 2026 and forecasters are
split on when that turns. With prices not running, the cost of trading houses — stamp duty,
agent fees, moving costs — is harder to justify, and more owners are choosing to improve the
home they already own. Custom window furnishings sit well on that list: they change how every
room looks and feels, do real thermal work morning and night, and are fitted in days rather
than renovation months. Note also that for most Australian family homes the main residence is
generally exempt from capital gains tax on sale, unlike an investment property — homeowners
should confirm their own position with their accountant.
